corrections.claimed_speedup: doc/benchmarks.md (Sept 2022, commit 315b2e52 v0.3.0-rc.1, i5-10210U), vs zlib 1.2.11: deflate decode 100k just_one_read 521 MB/s (clang11) / 522 MB/s (gcc10) vs 352 MB/s (1.48x); 100k many_big_reads 330 vs 277 MB/s (1.19x); 10k full_init 409 vs 289 MB/s (1.41x); 1k full_init 195 vs 241 MB/s (0.81x, slower). gzip decode 100k 527 MB/s clang11 (1.81x) / 550 MB/s gcc10 (1.89x); zlib-format decode 100k 505 MB/s clang11 (1.56x) / 548 MB/s gcc10 (1.70x). README: 'up to 1.4x faster than zlib-the-library (C)'.
corrections.caveats: Numbers are from Sept 2022 (zlib 1.2.11, v0.3.0-rc.1) and first-party, though reproducible. Slower than zlib on 1 KB inputs (0.76x-0.93x). The same page lists libdeflate 1.7.1: faster than Wuffs at 1k (326 MB/s) and 10k (503 MB/s), slightly slower at 100k just_one_read (507 vs 521 MB/s). Baseline is zlib, not zlib-ng. Language is Wuffs, consumed as generated single-file C.

corrections.caveats: Rust crate, not C++; baselines are Rust varint implementations (prost, rustc_serialize LEB128, integer-encoding-rs), not a C/C++ varint or protobuf library. rustc version unstated. Single-integer LEB128 varint, not block bit-packing. Requires SSSE3 minimum and x86_64 only (no NEON, no scalar fallback). Uses a lot of unsafe code; the fastest column is the 'unsafe' interface that skips overflow and bounds checks (safe decode u32: 332.11 vs prost 196.05). Last commit 2024-09-03.
